subject: existing-runtime online repair bridge, supervisor status handshake and Local handoff
repaired_findings: durable worker intent now precedes the sole provider-facing worker call; repeated or lost-ack execution is status-only and cannot redispatch
request-scoped dedicated scientific project plus exact registration prevents the queue-wide worker from selecting an unrelated project task
runtime/adapter bytes, DB device/inode, full request, project, campaign, failed plan, supervisor observation and task evidence are hash/identity bound and rechecked
deterministic repairs/<campaign>/<request>/ output namespaces reject unowned pre-intent outputs and never auto-apply patches
campaign-wide budget identity and immutable per-request reservation receipts prevent per-request projects from resetting the retained repair allocation
campaign reservation precedes enqueue, so rejected/corrupt allocation state or a process interruption cannot leave executable unreserved work in the runtime queue
native adapter, GPU authority, scientific retry, changed capability inventory and output overwrite are rejected
registration, budget-reservation and enqueue intents/results plus worker/failure/reconciliation records are immutable events with an append-only journal; later status cannot overwrite prior evidence

the provider-facing worker begins same-session POSIX process-group teardown at the reserved max_seconds; timeout/transport loss retains termination evidence and bounded partial-output hashes as worker_unknown and later execution is status-only
the literal supervisor campaign and selected-entry envelope are schema-checked and a failed receipt must carry the selected campaign plan digest
retained JSON symlinks/nonregular files and malformed/negative budget reservations fail closed
supervisor observation validates retained append-only manifest/extension ancestry, so a repair admitted against a valid parent campaign remains attributable after later exact-reviewed extension

repair request observation takes a nonblocking shared owner lock and treats active, incomplete, unindexed, unknown-status and durable-intent-without-terminal-event states as reconciliation-required without racing the bridge writer

every retained event filename/content/request digest, ordered sequence/previous-event hash, journal order and last-status pointer are reconciled; tamper or ambiguity fails closed rather than inferring success from wall-clock order
a retained registration, reservation, enqueue or worker intent forbids automatic replay; bridge rerun makes only the bounded authoritative runtime status call and retains reconciliation evidence

supervisor observation mirrors the bridge's immutable request-admission contract: live runtime/adapter hashes and DB identity, dedicated project policy and limits, complete failed-campaign/plan/receipt/status evidence, cumulative budget, inputs/instructions, dedicated outputs and exact task are all rebound before any status is reported

only the ordered registration-to-budget-to-enqueue-to-worker progression is accepted; exact stage/worker intents, invocation argv/outcomes, predecessor evidence and reservation identity are required, while incomplete or mutated evidence is reconciliation-required or rejected
an existing dedicated output without durable worker intent is classified as unowned reconciliation-required state, matching the bridge's first-dispatch preflight refusal
extension mutation does not perform a new fallible bridge scan after committing state; it returns readback_required and leaves detailed status to a separate read-only observation
documentation distinguishes task contracts from OS confinement and records the source-authored supervisor handshake separately from an actually configured/qualified worker
remaining_important: Local has not run the generated tests, the real retained bridge-to-supervisor observation path, or the actual installed runtime/SQLite/ACP/provider integration path; source fixtures prove control flow only

the initial repair-budget amount and terminal code-error classification remain trusted Local review/authorization boundaries; the bridge enforces their exact bytes and cumulative use but cannot infer user authority from repository files

DB device/inode detects path replacement but not an in-place controller reinitialization; Local must bind and return actual runtime status/events/controller identity because this runtime guide exposes no controller UUID in the request contract
